Tax should use banker's rounding (`decimal.ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). Halves round to the nearest even number, so 2.5 becomes 2 and 3.5 becomes 4. Don't use `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

That rule comes from a project memory (`.engramdb/memories/tax-uses-round-half-even_…md`), not from the code. The memory says it was agreed with the finance team in March 2026 and was written by a person.

The code doesn't implement any rounding for tax yet. In `src/billing/tax.py:11`, `tax_for(amount_cents, rate)` only raises `NotImplementedError`. `Decimal` is imported but never used, and the tests only cover `line_total`. Nothing in the code currently enforces half-even, so whoever writes `tax_for` needs to apply it, for example with `Decimal(...).quantize(Decimal("1"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN)` on the cents value.
